import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import SeqDiagram from '../../../../components/SeqDiagram.astro';

**Task:** announce that something changed so clients can react.

## Declare the events

An `#[app::event]` enum in the `#[app::logic]` module. The variant name is the
event name; the fields are its data (camelCase keys; `u64`, `i64` and bytes as
strings). From `apps/kv-store`:

```rust
#[app::event]
pub enum Event {
    /// A new key was stored.
    Inserted { key: String, value: String },
    /// An existing key's value was replaced.
    Updated { key: String, value: String },
    /// A key and its value were removed.
    Removed { key: String },
    /// Every key was removed from a non-empty store.
    Cleared,
}
```

The events and their fields are listed in the app's [ABI](/build/app-abi/).

## Emit them

```rust
pub fn update_if_exists(&mut self, key: String, value: String) -> app::Result<bool> {
    if !self.entries.contains(&key)? {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    let _old = self.entries.insert(&key, &value)?;
    env::emit(Event::Updated { key, value }, Audience::All)?;
    Ok(true)
}
```

`env::emit(event, audience)` adds the event to the run's outcome. It reaches
clients only if the call succeeds and its entry commits; a failed call emits
nothing. `env::emit_raw(name, &data, audience)` emits any serde value by name.

## Choose the audience

| `Audience` | Receives it |
| --- | --- |
| `All` | Everyone subscribed to the app. |
| `Caller` | The caller of the run. |
| `Accounts(vec![..])` | These accounts. |
| `Team(id)` | The members of a team. |
| `Org` | The members of the app's org. |
| `OrgAdmins` | The admins of the app's org. |

The node resolves the audience when it delivers, against the org at that
moment.

## Read them

Clients follow `GET /apps/{app}/events?from=N`: server-sent events, the
committed events from log index `N`, then live ones, each sent only to the
accounts its audience names ([Node API](/operate/admin-api/)). mero-js and
calimero-client-py wrap the stream, and a [typed client](/build/guides/typed-clients/)
types each event; `meroctl` prints it:

```sh
meroctl context watch my-kv --from 0      # --limit N to stop after N events
```

<SeqDiagram id="d-build-events" title="From emit to a subscribed client"
  lanes={[
    { label: 'Writer', color: '#f0883e' },

    { label: 'Any replica', color: '#39d0d8' },
    { label: 'Subscriber', color: '#3fb950' },
  ]}
  steps={[
    { from: 4, to: 3, label: 'GET /apps/{app}/events?from=N (SSE)' },
    { from: 0, to: 1, label: 'POST /apps/{app}/intents set' },
    { from: 1, to: 2, label: 'handle(call, "set", args)' },
    { from: 2, to: 2, label: 'env::emit(Updated, Audience::All)' },
    { from: 2, to: 1, label: 'Ok + writes + events', dashed: true },
    { from: 1, to: 3, label: 'one Raft entry: diff and events' },
    { from: 1, to: 0, label: 'result, index, the events it may see', dashed: true },
    { from: 3, to: 3, label: 'commit: resolve each audience' },
    { from: 3, to: 4, label: 'event: Updated {key, value}', dashed: true },
  ]} />

A client that renders state from a view and then follows the stream passes
`from` = the view's `index + 1`, so it misses nothing and sees nothing twice.

<Aside type="note">
  To make another app react, send it a [cross-app call](/build/guides/cross-context/)
  instead: an event is for clients.
</Aside>
